verses.1: Oh foolish Galatians! Who has chosen you? Who were those whom Jesus Christ, the crucified One, wrote down in His eyes?
verses.2: This is all I want to learn from you: whether the spirit of law comes from legal actions, or from faith through listening.
verses.3: Are you really that stupid? Have you already begun to be destroyed by the spirit of flesh?
verses.4: Have you suffered so much for this? Perhaps it really is true.
verses.5: So, by offering you the Holy Spirit and by exercising within you the powers of law or faith through your actions.
verses.6: Just as Abraham believed in God, so too should we believe in Him with righteousness.
verses.7: Therefore, remember that those who are from the faith, these are the sons of Abraham.
verses.8: It is also written that because of faith, God has announced to Abraham that all nations will be blessed in him.
verses.9: So that those who are righteous may be blessed along with the faithful Abraham.
verses.10: For those who violate the laws of the law, they are indeed condemned. It is written that they are all condemned, as they do not follow the rules stated in the book of laws regarding how to act.
verses.11: For in the law, it is clear that no one deserves to live before God. The righteous will live because of their faith.
verses.12: But this law isn’t based on faith; rather, those who enforce it will live according to it.
verses.13: Christ has explained to us the suffering that arises from the laws that govern us. It is said that “Every one who climbs onto a tree becomes a victim of its own law.”
verses.14: That the righteousness of Abraham may be known among all nations through Christ Jesus, so that we may receive the message of the Spirit through faith.
verses.15: Brothers, I say this in human terms. But no one should tamper with or violate the sacred covenant of humanity.
verses.16: But to Abraham were revealed these words, as well as his seed. It’s not said “to all seeds,” but rather “to one seed alone.” And that seed is Christ.
verses.17: And I say this: A covenant that has been broken by God still remains valid for four hundred and thirty years, so that it cannot be abolished.
verses.18: For if inheritance is based on law, then it is no longer based on revelation. But God has chosen Abraham through revelation.
verses.19: What is this law then? It was established for the purpose of preventing violations. This applies until the seed is given birth, according to the commands given through messengers in the hands of intermediaries.
verses.20: But one mediator is not enough; the God is one.
verses.21: Is this indeed a law regarding the messages of God? It didn’t happen. For if such a law were given to those who have power over people, then justice would indeed be based on that law.
verses.22: But it also sealed off everything through sin, so that the message of faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
verses.23: Before the payment was made according to the law, we stood together, waiting for the payment to be revealed.
verses.24: So that the law became a teacher for us, leading us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
verses.25: When faith comes into play, it is no longer controlled by those who manipulate people.
verses.26: For all of God’s children are united in faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.27: For those who have been baptized in Christ, they have put on Christ’s robe.
verses.28: Neither a Jew nor a Greek, neither a slave nor a free man, neither an enemy nor a friend. For all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
verses.29: But if you are the descendants of Christ, then your ancestors’ seed indeed constitutes your heritage, according to the prophecy.
